title: Policy Tuner Canvas — micro‑presets + explainability overlay for cache & batch settings
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a single, composable canvas in the Redwood Console where operators can create and preview small, targeted 'micro‑presets' that tune caching and batching parameters for a route or model. The canvas surfaces an explainability overlay that shows estimated latency/cost/quality deltas, highlights guardrail violations, and enables a simulated traffic run before rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas allows creating, editing, duplicating, and deleting micro‑presets for batching and cache settings
Explainability overlay displays estimated token cost, P50/P95 latency change, and an estimated quality score delta for each preset
Guardrail badges surface critical issues (e.g., increased token inflation >15%, cache key collisions, unsafe prefix caching) with contextual remediation links
Simulator can run a sampled workload and show timeline visualization of batching behavior and cache hit/miss heatmap
Exportable JSON policy and one‑click create rollout (canary) button that ties to existing rollouts API
Accessibility: overlay information is screen‑reader readable and color contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA
design_notes: Micro‑presets: short, named configs (Goal: target a specific optimization e.g., 'latency‑fast', 'cost‑conservative', 'prefill‑safe')
Explainability overlay: three stacked bars for cost/latency/quality with +/- percentage and absolute estimates sourced from the Optimize estimator service
Simulate mode uses a 1k sample of recent traffic (configurable) with synthetic KV cache warmup to approximate hit rates
Guardrails are triaged into Severity: Critical (block rollout), Warning (requires ack), Info
Primary CTA pattern: 'Preview Simulation' -> modal with time slider -> 'Create Canary' (prepopulates rollout targets)
Persisted history: every preset saves a changelog entry with author and timestamp for auditability
decisions: Use existing Optimize estimator API rather than a client‑side heuristic to keep estimates consistent with backend billing models
Limit presets visible on route main page to 4 most recent to reduce cognitive load — rest available in 'All Presets' drawer
Simulation will be asynchronous (job) with a cached results artifact so engineers can re‑run without re‑sampling production traffic
Guardrail 'block' level will prevent direct canary creation; user must acknowledge and add a mitigation or select a safer preset
review_feedback: PM (Owen Patel) — request: show explicit rollback ETA for canary (how long before automatic fallback) and include cost delta across the entire canary cohort
Eng Lead (Aisha Malik) — note: simulator should expose sampling seed and be able to rehydrate KV cache snapshot from last warmup run for reproducibility
Security (Ravi Kapoor) — ensure simulator sampling removes PII and that exportable policy JSON does not include customer secrets or KMS identifiers
UX Research (Lena Smirnova) — suggested 3‑user test sessions focusing on comprehension of the explainability overlay microcopy
